summaries.summary: Deep neural networks (DNNs), particularly convolutional and recurrent neural networks with huge architectures, have succeeded in tasks including audio processing such as speech to text, emotion recognition, and speech/non-speech classification.

Training deep architectures requires large annotated data, limiting low data resource scenarios common in speech-based applications, where annotation is difficult and emotion recognition suffers from annotator disagreement.

This work proposes simultaneous two sample learning (s2sL), which trains a classifier using two samples simultaneously for classification in low data resource scenarios and low resource data imbalance.
The s2sL approach for low data resource problems is explained using MLP, modified to handle the data representation, as the base classifier for a two-class classification task.
For a two-class classification task with INLINEFORM0 class labels and INLINEFORM1 and INLINEFORM2 samples, classifiers are generally trained using input-output pairs as DISPLAYFORM0.

INLINEFORM0 is the INLINEFORM1-dimensional feature vector for the INLINEFORM2 sample with INLINEFORM3 class label, and simultaneous two sample (s2s) representation considers two samples as DISPLAYFORM0.

INLINEFORM0 and INLINEFORM1 are INLINEFORM2-dimensional feature vectors for the INLINEFORM3 sample in INLINEFORM4 class and INLINEFORM5 sample in INLINEFORM6 class, with INLINEFORM7 and INLINEFORM8 as output labels.
In s2s data representation, the input feature vector has length INLINEFORM0, output class labels are INLINEFORM2 or INLINEFORM3, and train samples increase to INLINEFORM5 from INLINEFORM6 samples.
MLP is the base classifier used to validate the proposed s2s framework, and modifications to its architecture are made to train on s2s based data representation.
The input layer has INLINEFORM0 units instead of INLINEFORM1 units to accept INLINEFORM2 and INLINEFORM3 simultaneously.
The hidden layer resembles a regular MLP, with hidden units varied from 2 to INLINEFORM0, a single hidden layer considered, and Rectified linear units (ReLU) used.
The output layer has four units for two-class classification, uses sigmoid activation and binary cross-entropy, because s2s output labels have more than one active unit and cannot use softmax.

The s2s-MLP output layer has outputs INLINEFORM0 and INLINEFORM1, four units for two-class classification, possible labels INLINEFORM4, INLINEFORM5, INLINEFORM6, INLINEFORM7, and is trained using adam optimizer.
Generally, the feature vector corresponding to the test sample is provided as input to the trained MLP in testing, and the class label is decided from the obtained output.
In s2sL, the test sample feature vector is converted to s2s data representation by combining it with preselected reference samples whose class labels are known a priori, as DISPLAYFORM0.

INLINEFORM0 and INLINEFORM1 are INLINEFORM2-dimensional feature vectors for the test sample and INLINEFORM3 reference sample, INLINEFORM4 is the considered number of reference samples, and reference samples can come from either class.

Each test sample INLINEFORM0 is combined with all INLINEFORM2 reference samples to form INLINEFORM4 instances, and outputs INLINEFORM6 are combined by voting-based decision approach to obtain final decision INLINEFORM9.

Preliminary results validate s2sL on Speech/Music discrimination and emotion classification, using GTZAN Music-Speech dataset with 120 audio files, 60 speech and 60 music, and 13-dimensional MFCC vectors.

The standard Berlin speech emotion database (EMO-DB) has 535 utterances corresponding to 7 different emotions, with 19-dimensional feature vectors from WEKA toolkit on 384-dimensional openSMILE toolkit vectors.

All experimental results use 5-fold cross validation with 80% training and 20% testing, 4 training data proportions, Accuracy (in %) for balanced tasks, and INLINEFORM6 for imbalanced Anger/Happy emotion classification.
Table TABREF14 shows mean accuracies (in %) from 5-fold cross validation, where s2sL outperforms MLP for Speech/Music and Neutral/Sad classification, especially at low resource conditions.

Table TABREF14 shows s2sL outperforms MLP, Eusboost and MWMOTE on imbalanced Anger/Happy classification, with around 3 % absolute improvement in INLINEFORM1 over MWMOTE and 6% ( INLINEFORM3 ) improvement in INLINEFORM4.

The paper introduced a novel s2s framework that learns class discriminative characteristics from low data resources, considers two samples simultaneously, generates multiple test instances using preselected reference samples, and handles low resourced data imbalance.
